system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — USG Corporation realized record after merger with Gebr. Knauf KG, ~3-5-year horizon (~2022-2024)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private by a foreign
> (German) acquirer and deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; the
> traceable realized record is limited to the deregistration filing and reputable press.
> This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On May 6, 2019, USG Corporation filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of
  registration of its common stock and preferred stock purchase rights under Section
  12(g) of the Exchange Act (and/or suspension of its duty to file reports under
  Sections 13/15(d)), recording approximately 1 holder of record as of the certification
  date. [SRC: SEC accession 0000757011-19-000068, Form 15-12B]
- A search of USG Corporation's (CIK 0000757011) EDGAR filing history for annual reports
  (Form 10-K, Form 20-F) in each of 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024 returns no filings;
  the last periodic filings on the registrant's record are from the closing period
  (February 2019 10-K covering FY2018, and the April-May 2019 closing/deregistration
  filings). [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000757011&type=10-K]
- Knauf (Gebr. Knauf KG) is a privately held German limited partnership that does not
  file periodic reports with the SEC; no source was found in which Knauf separately
  discloses the acquired USG business's post-close financial trajectory for the
  ~2022-2024 window. [UNVERIFIED]
- No public audited financial statements (10-K/20-F or equivalent) are available for the
  acquired USG business for the ~2022-2024 window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Documented factual events within the ~2022-2024 window (press-sourced)
- In a related joint-venture business associated with the transaction — USG Boral, the
  Asia-Pacific plasterboard and ceilings joint venture in which Knauf acquired full
  ownership in connection with the 2019 merger — the "USG Boral" brand name was
  reported to be gradually replaced by the "Knauf" brand in Australia during 2022,
  according to a distributor's news post dated February 28, 2022 quoting Knauf's
  Australian managing director; the post states this was a name/branding change only,
  with the business continuing to supply the same product range from the same
  manufacturing facilities. [SRC: https://www.nhs.trade/news/post/usg-boral-rebrands-as-knauf.html]
- This rebranding item concerns the Asia-Pacific joint-venture business, not USG's core
  U.S. gypsum/wallboard operations, and no source was found isolating a comparable
  documented event specifically for the U.S. business within the ~2022-2024 window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Items noted but outside the fixed outcome window
- Reputable press reported that USG (by then part of the Knauf Group since 2019) would
  permanently close its Southard, Oklahoma manufacturing facility in November 2026,
  affecting more than 250 employees, phasing out the majority of a specialized
  industrial-gypsum-products portfolio; the press report states the facility had
  continued operating under Knauf ownership since 2019 and attributes the closure to
  "escalating complexity and cost to mine and manufacture the specialized products in
  the portfolio." This event falls well outside the ~2022-2024 fixed outcome window
  (announced 2026) and is noted here only for completeness, not as an in-window outcome
  fact. [SRC: https://www.wconline.com/articles/98512-usg-to-close-oklahoma-plant-250-jobs-affected]

## Items sought but not found
- No reputable-press or primary source was located reporting a divestiture, impairment,
  write-down, bankruptcy, or comparable financial outcome scalar specifically tied to
  the Knauf-owned former-USG U.S. gypsum business within the ~2022-2024 window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because USG Corporation was acquired by a privately held foreign (German) company and
  deregistered its securities in May 2019, there is no public audited outcome record
  (10-K/20-F) for the ~2022-2024 window for the acquired business itself. [SRC: SEC accession 0000757011-19-000068, Form 15-12B]
- The only in-window documented factual item found concerns a brand-name change (not a
  financial or operational scalar) in a related Asia-Pacific joint-venture business, not
  the core acquired U.S. entity. [SRC: https://www.nhs.trade/news/post/usg-boral-rebrands-as-knauf.html]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome: the
  absence of a public periodic-reporting record for the acquired business precludes a
  sourced determination of its realized 3-5-year financial or operational trajectory.

[SLICE END]
